editorial: Cambodia was fairly affordable. We did benefit from visiting in non-peak times, but even the most popular months are not too exorbitant.

Excluding flights into and out of Siem Reap, our trip consisting of two nights cost us $440 for two people. The good news is USD is acceptable in most of Siem Reap, so you don’t have to fret about carrying Cambodian riel.
Tourism does subsidise the rest of the economy in Siem Reap, so expect the food in particular to be expensive relative to what’s on offer.

categories.title: Stays
editorial: Pandora Suite d’Angkor, a cute little hotel with a pool, cost us around $30 per night. Once again, we saved money by avoiding the peak season. A cursory Google search tells me you could spend ~50% more than we did.

categories.title: Food & Drinks
editorial: We spent about $100 on meals, which is a lot of money for two days in a country with a GDP per capita under $3,000. And this does not include the buffet we had as part of the Apsara dance show.
We didn’t have a lot of alcohol or party hard, so can’t really say what that costs.

categories.title: Experiences
editorial: Tickets to Angkor Wat cost us $75 (or $37 each), while the tour was $28 (or $14 each). Pretty reasonable for a World Heritage Site! We had a wonderful guide, so a $20 tip only felt right.
The Apsara dance and buffet dinner set us back $70 (or $35 each). But it’s a worthwhile expense to immerse in Cambodian tradition as well as the best food we had on our trip.

categories.title: Inter-City Travel
editorial: None in our case, but we did spent $8 per person on the bus from the airport to our hotel and $30 for the Grab taxi back to the airport.

categories.title: Miscellaneous
editorial: We needed visas for Cambodia, which was $30 per head.
In addition to the other expenses, you’ll need to account for SIM cards.

alternatives.title: What if we had a bigger budget?
editorial: Even with a bigger budget, we wouldn’t do much different. There’s only so much Siem Reap has to offer. Perhaps we’d tip our guide more handsomely!

alternatives.title: What if we had a smaller budget?
editorial: If things are tight, we recommend carrying your own food particularly since it’s a short trip. You can also skip the Apsara dance performance if you think the cost is too steep.
